cvEn:
Tuval Yaakov (Tobi) Tsanani, son of Michal and Tsuriel, was born on the 28th of Av 5763 (26 August 2003) in Moshav Zavdiel, near Kiryat Gat. He was the second of three children, brother to Ravid and Avia.

Tuval grew up in Kiryat Gat. He was a charming, pleasant, cheerful and modest boy. He always showed respect to others and considered the good of the other. His mother related: "The sound of his name was the essence of who he was. One of his nicknames was Tobi, for the simple reason that he was a child who was all goodness. From a very young age he was busy with volunteering and doing."

He was educated in Kiryat Gat, at an elementary school and at the ORT Shalhevet Aviation and Space High School. In seventh grade he was chosen to take part in the "Squadron" programme, where he stood out for his strong desire to contribute. He is remembered as the only student at the school who remained active in it until tenth grade. In ninth grade he grew his hair in order to donate it to cancer patients, and in twelfth grade he carried out his intention: he cut his hair and donated it.

His greatest love was Magen David Adom, where he felt most whole and influential. He began volunteering there in tenth grade through the "Personal Commitment" project, first as a trainee and later as an instructor. He also served as the Magen David Adom representative on the Kiryat Gat municipal youth council.

Beyond his studies, he volunteered in the Ministry of Education's "Young Instructors" programme (Madatzim), in the "Young Instructors of Home Front Readiness" programme (Mashatzim), and in the youth movement Ahrayim, where he started as a member and later accompanied pupils in their preparations for meaningful service in the IDF. He was active in the "Ramon Foundation" excellence programme and was the first trainee there to become an instructor.

In eleventh grade he received a national ORT award for his social involvement and contribution to his community in his city, and he was chosen as one of the "Stars of ORT", young leaders who pave the way in contributing to the community and society.

His mother said his giving was so great that he sometimes had to be reminded to stop and do something for himself so he could recharge, but he would reply with a smile: "The more you give, the more you receive."

His sister said she had learned from him to volunteer and help. He pushed her to achieve her goals, comforted her when she cried, taught her to see the good in everything, and told her that every obstacle is "just an obstacle on the way to a leap forward."

Tuval excelled in his talent for playing the guitar. His music teacher said: "You had the soul of an artist, gentle and sensitive, which only a few are blessed with. You played the guitar in a captivating way, and through it you expressed your feelings and emotions. Music was for you a tool for connecting with people, and we often heard you playing during breaks, surrounded by students from different age groups, detached from the material world, diving into the sounds and melodies you created."

Another talent of his was cooking, and there too there was giving, because the dishes he cooked brought joy to those who tasted them. As a teenager, on Friday mornings he would ride his bicycle in nature, photograph the landscape, and enjoy the sunrise with a thermos of coffee at the top of the hill.

Whenever he had the chance, he cared for his three dogs, and he was devoted to other dogs as part of his work as a dog handler (dogwalker). After finishing his studies and until his enlistment, he worked at a McDonald's branch, where he was considered a devoted and very orderly worker who aspired to advance there.

On 28 March 2022 he enlisted in the IDF and joined the Armored Corps. After completing his training as a gunner, he was posted to the 53rd Battalion of the Barak Division (188th Brigade).

At the beginning of his military service he wrote a long text, full of sincerity and humour, describing what it means to be an armored soldier. It included the following: "When you tell people 'I'm in the Armored Corps,' what do they think? They think you miss your family. Honestly, they're not wrong. Everyone here misses their second family. But your real family, the one you earned with blood, sweat and grease, is always with you... Being an armored soldier is more than just riding in a tank, more than sleeping in your overalls for a whole week without taking off your boots or changing your underwear. It's even more than the firepower you operate at the push of a button.

Being an armored soldier means many things, like professionalism and discipline. But being an armored soldier, in the bottom line, is comradeship, a small word with a great meaning. It means loving your friend with all your heart, being ready to die for him without thinking twice, hugging him and crying with him... It means knowing what your friend feels just from the slightest movement of his back. It means fighting with your crew and almost coming to blows, but in the end giving fun and a smile and forgetting everything. Because being an armored soldier means being part of a large family."

As a soldier, too, he did not abandon his volunteering with Magen David Adom. When he came home for Shabbat after weeks in the army, he showed up there for shifts. To save lives, he gave up Shabbat meals with his family and his weekend rest.

He adopted John Lennon's quote as his motto for life: "Everything will be all right in the end. If it's not all right, it means it's not yet the end." He would often say that "anger is an emotion that wastes time."

On Shabbat, 22 Tishrei, Simchat Torah 5784, 7 October 2023, at half past six in the morning, the terrorist organization Hamas launched a surprise attack on Israel. Under cover of massive barrages of missiles and rockets from the Gaza Strip into wide areas of the country, thousands of terrorists broke into Israel by land, sea and air, and launched a murderous assault on the communities of the Gaza envelope, on Sderot, Ofakim and Netivot, on the music festival at the Re'im nature park near Kibbutz Re'im and Nir Oz, on IDF bases, and on travelers on the roads in the area. The terrorists murdered some eight hundred civilians in their homes and cars, after committing grave atrocities against them. They abducted hundreds of Israelis to the Gaza Strip and destroyed, looted and set fire to homes and property. Hundreds of soldiers, police officers, security personnel and members of local emergency squads fell in the battle. That morning, a war began.

Tuval's unit took part in the fighting from its outset. Among his activities as a fighter, he took part in operational activity in Shejaiya in eastern Gaza and in the Zeitoun neighborhood with the 13th Battalion of the Golani Brigade, and took part in various operations. Although he suffered from severe swelling in his legs, he insisted on carrying out the operational activity with his comrades and gave up the rest that had been offered to him.

On 4 December 2023, during an operational activity in Shejaiya, his tank was hit by an anti-tank missile and he was killed.

Sergeant Tuval Yaakov (Tobi) Tsanani fell in battle on 21 Kislev 5784 (4 December 2023), at the age of twenty. He was laid to rest in the military cemetery in Kiryat Gat. He left behind parents, a brother and a sister.

After his fall he was posthumously promoted to Staff Sergeant.

His father eulogized him: "Our Tobi, flower of the family, a charming, beloved and smiling boy, our pain is unbearable... Everyone loved you, whether in volunteering at Magen David Adom, or afterwards. Our child, the crown of our heads, the beloved of our hearts, we were given you as a gift for a borrowed time... twenty summers of happiness, joy, delight and pride. Thank you, child, for choosing us to be your parents. Forgive us for not managing to protect you... We love you, dear son, our private hero; we will continue to fight in your place."

His brother Ravid eulogized him: "You were so good while you were here with us. You were always welcoming, smiling, and everywhere you went people loved you... We built dreams together, we hoped to fulfil them, to travel together, to walk together, to start a family... I love you, I'm proud of you, you are the pride of the home, and of the entire Jewish people... Dear man, dear brother, thank you for the time I was privileged to be your big brother and to guide you. I miss you; watch over all of us from above."

His sister Avia eulogized him: "Our Tobi, you will always be with us. You are my guardian. I love you to the end of the universe and back. I will commemorate you forever as my brother, my hero and the hero of everyone who knew you. When I have children, I will raise them in your image."

Magen David Adom and its donors placed an ambulance in his memory at the Magen David Adom station in Kiryat Gat.

The song "HaNigun Shebecha" (The Melody Within You) was written in his memory, based on a melody he composed, which was found after his death. It appears as an animated clip on YouTube (music: Tuval Tsanani; lyrics: Yitzhak Sviisa and Pariel Levi; performed by Uri Oz).

Tuval is commemorated on the "Remember" and "Filling the Void" websites, and on the website of the ORT network, through which he studied.

At ORT Shalhevet, the school where he was educated, a memorial room was established, and an award ceremony for students excelling in social involvement was dedicated to his memory. On the first anniversary of the outbreak of the war, a race was held at the school in his memory, with pupils running alongside soldiers of his battalion. The race is planned to take place every year.

At the Magen David Adom station in Kiryat Gat, a memorial corner for Tuval was established, and an ambulance was donated to the station in his memory by friends of Magen David Adom. The family initiated a donation of defibrillators, which were given to all the city's first responders and for use across the Lachish region.
